description: Fail-loudly CSV parser and editor: names the record and field, never repairs
notes: Installed as csv2.exe. Verify with:  csv2 --version
REQUIRES the Swift runtime of the version that BUILT THE RELEASE YOU GET, which
Scoop does not install. Look at the version this manifest installs:
csv2 0.1.3  was built with Swift 6.3.3  -> needs Runtimes\6.3.3\usr\bin on PATH
csv2 0.1.4  was built with Swift 6.4.0  -> needs Runtimes\6.4.0\usr\bin on PATH
(both come from the swift.org installer of that version). With another runtime
version csv2 prints NOTHING and exits 0xC0000139 (127 from bash/zsh).
The archive is .tar.zst; Scoop unpacks it with the zstd it ships.
Verified on 2026-10-07 by running `scoop update csv2` on Windows 11: the hash
checked ok, and `csv2 --version` prints csv2 0.1.3 (v0.1.3 / fa2e792) from bash,
cmd.exe and zsh. `--headers 0 -append` on a file whose data holds a comma now
If csv2 was placed by install.zsh before, run `./install.zsh --uninstall` first:
Scoop overwrites that shim. After this, install.zsh refuses to write over it.
Only 64bit is published: an archive is built on the machine that built the binary,
and only that arrangement lets the version inside it be checked by running it.
